meta.title: Single-SNP trait associations
meta.description: Seven well-established, consumer-array-covered single-SNP traits. Each entry lists the effect allele, its dosage-keyed interpretations, and a citation. Alleles are given on the GRCh38 forward (plus / dbSNP reference) strand, matching how 23andMe and AncestryDNA report genotypes. Interpretation is withheld when the observed genotype contains an allele not expected at the locus.
meta.source: Effect alleles and directions verified individually against NCBI dbSNP (build 156, GRCh38.p14) and the cited primary literature.

traits.summary: The A allele tags the CYP1A2*1F 'fast metaboliser' variant; the C allele is the slower-metabolising form.

interpretations.2: Two copies of the fast (A) allele (AA): associated with faster caffeine clearance ('fast metaboliser'). Fast metabolisers tend to clear caffeine more quickly.
interpretations.1: One fast (A) and one slow (C) allele (AC): intermediate caffeine metabolism.
interpretations.0: No fast (A) allele (CC): associated with slower caffeine clearance ('slow metaboliser'). Slow metabolisers clear caffeine more slowly.

traits.citation: Cornelis MC et al. Coffee, CYP1A2 genotype, and risk of myocardial infarction. JAMA (2006). PMID:16522833
traits.note: An association, not a diagnosis. Caffeine response is also shaped by dose, tolerance, sleep, and other genes.

traits.summary: The A allele (the European -13910*T variant on the forward strand) keeps the lactase gene switched on into adulthood.

interpretations.2: Two persistence (A) alleles (AA): likely lactase-persistent (can typically digest lactose as an adult).
interpretations.1: One persistence (A) allele (AG): likely lactase-persistent (one copy is usually enough).
interpretations.0: No persistence (A) allele (GG): likely lactase non-persistent for this European variant. Note: other populations carry different persistence variants this SNP does not capture, so a GG result does not rule out tolerance.

traits.citation: Enattah NS et al. Identification of a variant associated with adult-type hypolactasia. Nat Genet (2002). PMID:11788828
traits.note: This SNP explains European lactase persistence. African and Middle-Eastern persistence variants are elsewhere and are not tested here.

traits.summary: This is one of three TAS2R38 sites that together form the taster (PAV) vs non-taster (AVI) haplotypes. It is used here as a PROXY for the haplotype. The G allele encodes proline (P), part of the taster haplotype.

interpretations.2: Two taster-tagging (G) alleles (GG): likely a 'taster' of bitter PTC/PROP compounds (proxy; assumes the common PAV/AVI haplotype pairing).
interpretations.1: One taster-tagging (G) allele (CG): often an intermediate taster (proxy).
interpretations.0: No taster-tagging (G) allele (CC): more likely a 'non-taster' of PTC/PROP (proxy).

traits.citation: Kim UK et al. Positional cloning of the human quantitative trait locus underlying taste sensitivity to phenylthiocarbamide. Science (2003). PMID:12595690
traits.note: PROXY only. Taster status is set by the full three-site TAS2R38 haplotype (rs713598, rs1726866, rs10246939); reading a single site can misclassify people carrying uncommon haplotypes.

traits.summary: The T allele (Gly180 loss of function) produces dry earwax and less apocrine body odour; the C allele produces wet earwax.

interpretations.2: Two dry-type (T) alleles (TT): dry earwax and typically reduced underarm body odour.
interpretations.1: One dry-type (T) allele (CT): usually wet earwax (the C/wet allele is dominant).
interpretations.0: No dry-type (T) allele (CC): wet earwax and typically more apocrine body odour.

traits.citation: Yoshiura K et al. A SNP in the ABCC11 gene is the determinant of human earwax type. Nat Genet (2006). PMID:16444273
traits.note: One of the cleanest single-gene traits in humans, but still a tendency, not a certainty.

traits.summary: The T allele is the R577X stop that switches off alpha-actinin-3 in fast-twitch fibres; the C allele (R577) keeps it working.

interpretations.2: Two stop (T) alleles (TT, 'XX'): no alpha-actinin-3. Common in the general population and over-represented in elite endurance athletes.
interpretations.1: One working and one stop allele (CT, 'RX'): mixed; the most common genotype.
interpretations.0: No stop (T) allele (CC, 'RR'): full alpha-actinin-3, over-represented in elite sprint/power athletes.

traits.citation: Yang N et al. ACTN3 genotype is associated with human elite athletic performance. Am J Hum Genet (2003). PMID:12879365
traits.note: A single gene nudges muscle fibre type; training, and dozens of other genes, matter far more for athletic performance.

traits.summary: This HERC2 site is the strongest single predictor of blue vs brown eyes. The G allele drives brown pigmentation; the A allele is permissive of blue eyes. This is PROBABILISTIC, not deterministic.

interpretations.2: Two brown-driving (G) alleles (GG): most likely brown eyes.
interpretations.1: One brown-driving (G) allele (AG): usually brown or intermediate (green/hazel) eyes.
interpretations.0: No brown-driving (G) allele (AA): most likely blue eyes, though other pigment genes can shift this.

traits.citation: Sturm RA et al. A single SNP in an evolutionary conserved region within intron 86 of the HERC2 gene determines human blue-brown eye color. Am J Hum Genet (2008). PMID:18252222
traits.note: PROBABILISTIC. Eye colour is polygenic; this one SNP predicts blue vs brown well but cannot call green/hazel reliably.

traits.summary: The A allele (ALDH2*2, Glu504Lys) cripples the enzyme that clears acetaldehyde after alcohol, causing facial flushing, nausea and rapid heartbeat. Common in East Asian ancestry.

interpretations.2: Two deficiency (A) alleles (AA): near-total ALDH2 deficiency; strong flushing and poor alcohol tolerance. People with this genotype are strongly advised to avoid alcohol.
interpretations.1: One deficiency (A) allele (AG): partial ALDH2 deficiency; noticeable flushing and elevated acetaldehyde after drinking.
interpretations.0: No deficiency (A) allele (GG): normal ALDH2 activity; typical alcohol metabolism.

traits.citation: Brooks PJ et al. The alcohol flushing response: an unrecognized risk factor for esophageal cancer from alcohol consumption. PLoS Med (2009). PMID:19320537
traits.health: HEALTH NOTE: ALDH2-deficient people (A allele) who drink alcohol have a substantially increased risk of oesophageal (squamous-cell) cancer, because acetaldehyde — a carcinogen — accumulates. This is a genuine, well-documented health consideration, not just a cosmetic 'Asian flush'. Discuss with a clinician if relevant.
